Corvo Engineering Pvt Ltd: Procurement Policy (PR to PO)
Document CORVO-PROC-POL-04 · Version 6.0 · Effective 1 November 2026 · Supersedes Version 5.0 · Owner:
Head of Procurement · Applies to plants PUN1 (Bhosari) and CHK1 (Chakan)
This policy decides what happens to every purchase requisition (PR) line raised in Corvo: whether
Procurement may place a purchase order (PO) directly, or must first run a sourcing event to get quotes. All
values are in INR, excluding GST.
1. Identifying the item
1.1 Every PR line must be matched to an item in the item master. If the requester gave an item
code, use it. If not, match the description to the item master (requesters often use short forms,
e.g. "brg 6205 2rs" for Ball bearing 6205-2RS).
1.2 A line that matches no item master item is a new item. It always goes to sourcing (route
NEW_ITEM_SOURCING), is never clubbed with other lines, and is valued at quantity × the
requester's estimated unit price.
2. Clubbing requirements (no splitting)
2.1 Splitting a requirement into several small PRs to stay under a limit is not allowed. Procurement
must therefore treat similar PR lines as one requirement and apply every limit in this policy to
the requirement's total value.
2.2 Take PR lines in order of creation time (then PR number, then line number). A line joins an
existing requirement when it is for the same item, for the same plant, was created within 10
calendar days of the requirement's first line, and its need-by date is within 5 days (either side) of
the first line's need-by date. Otherwise it starts a new requirement. If it could join more than one,
it joins the earliest.
2.3 The requirement date is the creation date of its first line. Contract validity and purchase history
are checked as of this date. If any line in the requirement is marked Emergency, the requirement
is an emergency.
3. Valuing a requirement
3.1 Requirement value = total quantity × unit price, where the unit price is the first of: (a) the rate of
the contract that will be used (4.3), or, if every applicable contract is out of ceiling, the lowest
applicable contract rate; (b) the price on the most recent PO for the item in the 365 days before
the requirement date; (c) the item master standard price.
4. Contracts
4.1 A rate contract applies to a requirement if the contract covers the item, the requirement date
falls between the contract's start and end dates (inclusive), and the contract supplier is Active in
the supplier master.
4.2 A contract can be used only while it has ceiling left: consumed value + this requirement's value
(at the contract rate) must not exceed the contract value ceiling. Requirements consume ceiling
in order of requirement date. Consumed values in the register are as at its last update; contracts
signed after that update start at zero.
4.3 If more than one contract applies, use the one with the lowest rate that still has enough ceiling.
4.4 The contract register is updated monthly. Contracts signed after the last update exist only as
signed PDF copies, and are binding from their start date.

5.8 Blocked or Inactive suppliers must never receive a PO or be suggested for a sourcing event.
6. Preferred supplier list
Procurement keeps a preferred supplier list for every item, built automatically from purchase history and
contracts and recalculated as of each requirement date.
6.1 Who is on the list: every Active supplier that has either (a) at least one PO for the item in the 365
days before the date, or (b) a contract covering the item that started on or before the date (even
if it has since expired).
6.2 Ranking: rank the suppliers on the list so that the best choice for a direct PO comes first.
Procurement looks at: how often we have bought the item from them, how recently, whether
they have held a contract for the item, and their on-time delivery and quality record.
Procurement leaves the exact weighting to the system design, but it must be consistent,
explainable to a buyer, and recorded. The top supplier is the 1st preferred supplier.
6.3 Reference price: the price on that supplier's most recent PO for the item in the 365 days; if it has
none, the rate in its most recent contract for the item.
6.4 Suggesting suppliers for sourcing: take the preferred list in order. If it has fewer suppliers than
needed (4 or 5), add other Active suppliers that list the item's category in the supplier master,
best delivery and quality record first. New items get no suggestions: the buyer finds suppliers.
7. Placing purchase orders (consolidation)
7.1 To reduce the number of POs, requirements that end in a PO are combined into one PO with
several lines when they have the same supplier, the same plant and the same route, and were
raised within 48 hours of the first requirement on that PO (measured from the creation time of
each requirement's first line).
7.2 Take requirements in order of creation time. A requirement joins the earliest open PO it qualifies
for; otherwise it starts a new PO. Sourcing requests are never combined.
Corvo Engineering · Procurement Policy v6.0 · page 2 of 3
8. Record keeping
8.1 Every decision must record the policy clause applied, and the contract or PO it relied on. A buyer
may override a decision only with a written reason, which is kept with the original decision.
9. Transition
9.1 This version applies to every requirement whose requirement date is on or after 1 November
2026. Requirements dated earlier remain under Version 5.0.
